record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: In the same terminal-free ball setting for a Steiner tree S_t, for t=1/2 or t∈(0,1), what is the largest possible number of branching points of S_t inside B_{tr}(x)?

evidence.quote: Question 2.6. What is the largest possible number of branching points of S_t in B_tr(x) for t=1/2 or other t∈(0;1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of points called terminals. A Steiner tree for $M$ is a connected set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of minimal total length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure) containing $M$. It is classical that any Steiner tree $S$ is a finite union of straight line segments meeting only at terminals or at so-called Steiner (branching) points; every branching point has degree exactly $3$ and the three incident segments meet pairwise at $120^\circ$ angles, while terminals have degree $1$, $2$, or $3$.

Fix a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a radius $r > 0$, and consider the closed ball $B_r(x)$. Assume that the Steiner tree $S$ has no terminal inside $B_r(x)$ (the "terminal-free ball" setting). For a parameter $t \in (0,1)$, consider the smaller concentric ball $B_{tr}(x)$.

Question: Over all finite terminal sets $M \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, all Steiner trees $S$ for $M$, and all balls $B_r(x)$ containing no terminal of $M$, what is the supremum (in particular for $t = 1/2$, and more generally for $t \in (0,1)$) of the number of branching (Steiner) points of $S$ contained in $B_{tr}(x)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers. No published resolution was located.
